hints: Look closely at how the chromosomes look in each photo. Which one has no thick, dark, individual chromosomes, just a dark fuzzy nucleus?
Remember DNA is copied by semi-conservative replication during the S phase of interphase, not while chromosomes are condensed for mitosis.
walkthrough:
**Spot what each photo shows**

Look at A, B and D first. You can see thick, condensed chromosomes. That tells you the cell is in mitosis and the nuclear envelope has broken down.

Photo C is different. It shows a round, intact nucleus with loose chromatin and no individual chromosomes. That is the classic look of interphase.

**Recall when DNA is replicated**

Semi-conservative replication doubles the DNA so each daughter cell gets a full copy. This happens in the S phase, which is part of interphase, well before mitosis starts.

**Match the process to the photo**

Since only photo C shows an interphase nucleus where the DNA is decondensed and accessible for copying, that is where replication takes place. So the answer is C.

options.A: Shows metaphase with chromosomes lined up on the equator. No DNA replication happens here, chromosomes are already duplicated.
options.B: Shows anaphase with sister chromatids pulled to opposite poles. DNA amount is being separated, not replicated.
options.C: Shows interphase with an intact nucleus and uncondensed chromatin. This includes S phase when semi-conservative DNA replication occurs.
options.D: Shows early mitosis (prophase) with condensing, visible chromosomes. Chromosomes condense after replication, so replication has already finished.
